docs.title: Step 1: Initial Setup
docs.text:
1. Login to Webex Control Hub (https://admin.webex.com)
  2. Go to Contact Center > AI Agents.
  3. Select Build your AI Agent,
  4. In the top right of the screen select + Create agent.
  5. You will see a list of templates. For today lets select Start from scratch and then Next
  6. Now select Autonomous
  7. Complete the configuration below:
  8. Agent name (Make this your name_business)
  9. AI engine (Set to Webex AI Pro 1.0)
  10. Agent Goal (Describe what this AI Agent will do)
  11. Click Create

docs.title: Step 2: AI Agent Configuration
docs.text:
1. Under AI Agent Configuration click on Profile
  2. Complete the Instructions field with step by step instructions for your agent to accomplish its goals Example: *- Summarize the user's request and ask them to confirm that you understood correctly.
  3. If necessary, seek clarifying details.
  4. Thank the user for their business and say goodbye.*
  5. Complete the Welcome Message field with the first message you want the AI Agent to say
  6. Click Save Changes

![A screenshot of a chat

AI-generated content may be incorrect.](assets/docx-image-005.png)

docs.title: Step 3: Build Knowledge Base
docs.text:
1. Click on Knowledge
  2. Click + Create Knowledge Base
  3. Enter a Knowledge Base Name (Make this your name) and then Create
  4. In Files you can drag and drop pdf, docx, txt, xlsx, xls or csv documents you want the AI Agent to learn and answer the customers query with
  5. In Documents you can click + Create Document
  6. Give it a Document name and then Add to new category and give the category a name
  7. In the document you can copy and paste any information you want the AI Agent to know about including images and flash pages

docs.title: Step 4: AI Agent Knowledge & Actions
docs.text:
• Go to Dashboard
  • Locate your AI Agent and click on it
  • Click on Knowledge and find your Knowledge base from the drop down menu
  • Click Save changes
  • Click Actions and then +New action
  • Action Name – Call it customer_information
  • Action description – explain to the AI Agent that this is the questions to ask the user if they are interested in signing up
  • Action Scope – Select Slot Filling and fulfillment
  • Under Slot Filling click + New input Entity
  • Entity name – name the field such as Customer_Name
  • Entity type – Select from the drop down menu the type of data you are gathering (Select String if its just customer name)
  • Entity description – In plain text enter a description of the field
  • Required – Set this to Yes
  • Repeat the previous step for all the information you want to collect from the customer
  • Under “Webex Connect Flow Builder Fulfillment”
  • Select Service – Set this to Webex_One_2025
  • Select Flow – Set this to AI Agent
  • Optional extra step is to go to https://raljawah1xsw.us.webexconnect.io/ and create your own service
  • Select Save
  • Once completed select Publish
  • Got to Language and select the language you would like your AI Agent to speak/chat in
  • Select Save Changes

docs.title: Step 5: Testing & Q&A
docs.text:
• In Dashboard select your AI Agent
  • Click Preview (Located top right of the screen)
  • Select Start a chat or Start a call
  • Edit profile, knowledge and Actions as required to make it perfect
  • Congratulations you are now a AI Developer!

  • Webex AI Agent Documentation
  • Webex Contact Center Developer Guide
  • Cisco Webex Community

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
In this interactive lab, you will learn how to build and deploy a fully functional Webex AI Agent. By the end of this session, you will:

  • Set up a Webex AI Agent from scratch.
  • Integrate the agent with Webex Contact Center.
  • Design simple yet effective conversation flows.
  • Test and optimize your AI Agent for immediate use.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text: Although the lab design and configuration examples could be used as a reference, for design related questions please contact your representative at Cisco, or a Cisco partner.

docs.title: Lab Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Webex Contact Center tenant access (Provided for you).
  • Basic familiarity with Webex Contact Center components.
  • A modern web browser (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox recommended).

docs.title: Lab Agenda (60 Minutes)
docs.text: Time Activity 0-5 min Welcome and Session Overview 5-10 min Introduction to Webex AI Agent and Architecture 10-25 min Initial Setup: Configure Webex AI Agent 25-40 min Designing Basic Conversation Flows 40-50 min Testing and Deploying the AI Agent 50-60 min Optimization Tips, Key Takeaways, and Q&A

docs.title: Adding user specific variables into your lab guide
docs.text: There may be times in which you want to embed some attendee specific information into the instructions of your lab guide, like credentials or phone numbers, which will be used on multiple pages of your lab guide. You can gather the information via a form or you can pass a pre-encoded JSON string as a URL parameter to populate the variable values into the browser's session storage. Then you can use a simple HTML tag with a special class name to update the values in the lab guide. This feature can be combined with the copy button method above.

docs.title: Form Method
URL Method
docs.text:
If you have a lot of attendee variables in your lab, you may choose to precompile and encode them so that you can simply provide a URL link which will load all of their required information.

docs.title: DOCX to Markdown script
docs.text: Use scripts/docx_to_markdown.py to convert a DOCX lab guide into markdown files.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Reads one .docx input file
  • Extracts all embedded images into docs/assets/ (or a custom assets directory)
  • Splits each Heading 1/Heading 2 that starts with Lab into its own markdown file in docs/
  • Writes all non-lab content to docs/non-lab.md

Important

Note

Optional arguments:

  • --docs-dir (default: docs)
  • --assets-dir (default: <docs-dir>/assets)

docs.title: Preparing your file
docs.text:
• The script will split your labs into separate files For heading levels 1 and 2 of your document if the text starts with the word Lab.
  • If you no not have the word Lab in the headings, the contents of that section will go into the non-lab.md file.
    • You can append the word Lab by using an advanced find and replace in Word to target the heading level and with the replace textbox containing Lab #: ^& for numbered labs then you can update the lab numbers
  • If you do not want your level 2 headings to be separate files, demote them to level 3 or lower.
    • If you plan to demote your level 2 heading so that you do not create separate files, make sure that you first demote level 3 to level 4 starting with the lowest level first to preserve your formatting.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• Open up a new terminal in the directory of this repo and if you are not already in the virtual environment, use the appropriate commands for your operating system listed below.
If you are on a PCIf you are on a Mac

In your terminal enter the following commands:

venv\Scripts\activate.ps1

In your terminal enter the following commands:

source venv/bin/activate

  • Locate the docx file you want to convert to Markdown, copy the path the the file into the box below and click the Update Lab Guide button. Path to File: Update Lab Guide
  • Copy this command into your terminal: python scripts/docx_to_markdown.py path/to/guide.docx

docs.title: After your files are created
docs.text:
• Add your files to the mkdocs.yml file in the nav section and save the file.
  • If you are not currently running mkdocs, start the server
  • Review your formatting and make any necessary adjustments

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text: This lab guide template uses MKDocs to take your markdown documentation and transform it into an interactive web based lab guide. You will need to install some software on your PC or Mac in order to take full advantage of the tool which will allow you to view your changes as you save them and ensure that your formatting is exactly how you want it.

docs.title: Publishing Your Changes
docs.text: As you progress with the creation of your lab guide, you should sync your changes periodically to GitHub.

docs.title: Syncing your changes to GitHub
docs.text:
Make sure that you have saved all of the files you want to sync up to the repository

Click the Source Control button in the left menu

Click the plus sign next to each file you want to sync as you hover over the file names or alternatively, click the plus sign next to changes

Enter a note about the changes you are making in the message text box

Click the down chevron on the commit button to reveal more options

Select Commit & Sync

docs.title: After you Sync your changes, it will take a few minutes for GitHub Actions to build the website so that you can view all of the changes you made.

Markdown All In One

Allows you to use common keyboard shortcuts for making text bold and italic without needing to memorize the Markdown syntax.
